# Lecture 2: The French Revolution
A lecture covering the French Revolution from its causes through its legacy.
## Timeline
- **1789**: Storming of the Bastille (July 14), National Assembly declared [source](hypatia://cite?file=french-revolution.mp4&t=75) - **1789-1792**: Constitutional Monarchy phase [source](hypatia://cite?file=french-revolution.mp4&t=380) - **1792-1794**: Radical Republic and Reign of Terror [source](hypatia://cite?file=french-revolution.mp4&t=510) - **1794**: Execution of Robespierre, end of Terror [source](hypatia://cite?file=french-revolution.mp4&t=510) - **1799**: Napoleon's coup d'état [source](hypatia://cite?file=french-revolution.mp4&t=795)
## Key Themes
- Economic crisis and inequality as revolutionary catalysts - The Declaration of the Rights of Man - The Napoleonic Code and modern citizenship
See also: [[louis-xvi]], [[robespierre]], [[napoleon-bonaparte]]

# Louis XVI
King of France whose reign ended with the Revolution. His extravagance and the economic crisis contributed to revolutionary sentiment [source](hypatia://cite?file=french-revolution.mp4&t=75).
See also: [[french-revolution-transcript]], [[robespierre]]

--- title: "Maximilien Robespierre" type: entity sources: [french-rev-file-id] tags: [french-revolution, reign-of-terror, politics] user_edited: false ---
# Maximilien Robespierre
Led the Committee of Public Safety during the Reign of Terror (1792-1794). Between 16,000 and 40,000 people were executed under his leadership [source](hypatia://cite?file=french-revolution.mp4&t=510). He was himself executed in July 1794.
See also: [[french-revolution-transcript]], [[napoleon-bonaparte]]

--- title: "Napoleon Bonaparte" type: entity sources: [french-rev-file-id] tags: [french-revolution, napoleon, france, military] user_edited: false ---
# Napoleon Bonaparte
Seized power in 1799 through a coup d'état, establishing the Consulate and later the First French Empire [source](hypatia://cite?file=french-revolution.mp4&t=795). Spread Revolutionary ideals across Europe through military conquest.
## Legacy
The Napoleonic Code influenced legal systems worldwide.
See also: [[french-revolution-transcript]], [[robespierre]]
